Colin Kaepernick. An American quarterback whose career was defined by both athletic excellence as a mobile player and activism around racial justice and police brutality. Drafted second round by the San Francisco 49ers in 2011, thirty-sixth overall, he became the starting quarterback in 2012. He led the 49ers to Super Bowl XLVII following the 2013 season, delivering exceptional performances in the playoffs. Through his career he threw for nearly ten thousand passing yards and eighty-eight touchdowns, and rushed for over two thousand three hundred yards with thirteen rushing touchdowns, making him a true dual threat. He made one Pro Bowl and earned All-Pro selection in 2013, his peak year before activism took center stage. In 2016, he began kneeling during the national anthem to protest police brutality and racial injustice, sparking national debate about sports activism. He then became a free agent and was effectively blackballed by NFL teams despite capable play, remaining a controversial figure whose activism led teams to pass on him despite his demonstrated NFL-caliber ability.
